territorial_scope.description: Applies to New Hampshire state law, reaching persons outside the state that conduct business in New Hampshire or target products or services to its residents.

evidence.quote: persons that conduct business in this state or persons that produce products or services that are targeted to residents of this state

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Chapter 507-H, enacted by SB 255 (2024), gives New Hampshire consumers rights over their personal data and imposes duties on controllers and processors that meet volume thresholds. It applies from 1 January 2025.
summary.long: Chapter 507-H applies from 1 January 2025 to persons doing business in New Hampshire, or targeting products to its residents, that control or process personal data of at least 35,000 unique consumers in a year, or 10,000 consumers with more than 25 percent of gross revenue from data sales. It excludes state bodies, nonprofits, higher education institutions, and certain financial and health-care entities. Consumers may access, correct, delete and port personal data and opt out of targeted advertising, data sales and certain profiling. Controllers must respond within 45 days, provide appeals, and honour opt-out preference signals from 1 January 2025. Controllers must limit collection, obtain consent for sensitive data, document data protection assessments for heightened-risk processing, and publish privacy notices. Processors act under written contracts. From 1 January 2027 controllers may not sell a child's personal data. The Attorney General has exclusive enforcement authority, with a 60-day cure period during 2025 and discretionary cure afterward. Violations are unfair or deceptive trade practices, and the chapter creates no private right of action.

notes: The text states no enabling act, amended instrument or repealed instrument; all relations are cross-references. Target instrument IDs are empty because no registry IDs were supplied. Drafting points: 507-H:4 II cites opt-out rights at 507-H:4, III(e), but the opt-out right is in I(e). 507-H:3 II(o) misspells HIPAA as HIPPA. The 507-H:9 heading reads De-Identifed Data. 507-H:6 I(e-1) is marked as effective January 1, 2027 (2026, 168:1). 507-H:12 refers to unnamed other law on third-party providers; no relation is recorded for it.
